Customer to share sample prompt set and multilingual test cases

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs

Benchmarks: latency, cost per token, and KV/prefix caching impact
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-04-02 15:00 PST | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Evan Carter (CTO - Polaris), Priya Sharma (ML Lead), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Mei Wong (PM)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood. quick note — we'll record, transcript on fireflies. how's everyone doing?
[00:09] Evan Carter: Doing good. thanks. excited to learn more.
[00:12] Priya Sharma: Hi — thanks. we sent over high-level requirements but want to dig into model selection — mainly context length, multi-lingual, and if we can do tool-calling reliably.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: Great, that's exactly what Maya and Carlos will walk through. Maya over to you?
[00:26] Maya Patel: Thanks Jordan. hi team, I lead Solutions at Redwood on inference. quick agenda: confirm current stack, perf targets, security, and then go through model tradeoffs for hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:36] Mei Wong: quick note — our product team expects consistent latency under 300ms for short queries and under 2s for streaming responses on longer flows. can't exceed 500ms tail for interactive.
[00:46] Maya Patel: good to call out. also helpful — what percent of traffic is multilingual and which languages?
[00:51] Priya Sharma: about 25% non-English. top languages are Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, and some Arabic. we also have long-context documents — up to 30k tokens for certain legal summary flows.
[01:05] Carlos Ruiz: ok so 30k context is notable. we support up to 32k+ context models; for hosted vs dedicated there are differences in available model variants and quantization profiles which affect latency and cost.
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: for Dedicated we need VPC peering and KMS integration — also audit logs stored for 7 years for compliance. is that supported?
[01:25] Maya Patel: yes, Dedicated and Private both support customer-managed KMS and long-term audit exports. Hosted has encrypted-at-rest and SOC 2 compliance but for KMS/HSM managed keys and long-term retention you’d choose Dedicated or Private.
[01:37] Evan Carter: what about data residency — we need EU-only for some customers.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: we can pin region routing and offer Private deployments for full on-prem. Dedicated can be hosted in EU regions, yes.
[01:46] Priya Sharma: back to models — we've benchmarked some open models but results vary. what do you recommend for multilingual and long context?
[01:55] Maya Patel: typically for 30k contexts we look at models with native 32k context windows — e.g., some open Llama-family variants and other 3rd-party 32k models. tradeoffs: larger context native models are heavier and cost more per token; an alternative is prefix-KV caching or chunking strategies.
[02:12] Priya Sharma: chunking loses global context for some tasks — legal summarization needs whole-doc reasoning.
[02:16] Carlos Ruiz: agreed. in that case native 32k models are best. for multilingual, some models are better out of the box — if Spanish/Portuguese/Japanese are high quality we recommend testing both a high-capacity multilingual model and a language-specialized one for those languages.
[02:32] Evan Carter: can Redwood host different models per route? like use a smaller cheaper model for embeddings and cheap completions and a big 32k model for long legal jobs?
[02:41] Maya Patel: yes — our routing supports per-route model pinning and automatic fallback. you can route by policy: latency first or cost first.
[02:47] Jordan Lee: quick question on tool-calling: do you need structured tool outputs or arbitrary function calling?
[02:52] Mei Wong: both. we use tool-calling to fetch internal customer records (via secure connector) and also need deterministic JSON outputs for downstream parsers.
[02:59] Carlos Ruiz: we support function calling / tool invocation with structured output hooks. caveat: deterministic outputs depend on prompt engineering and model choice — some models provide more stable JSON. we can add post-call validators and fallback rules.
[03:14] Priya Sharma: any differences hosted vs dedicated for tool-calling?
[03:18] Maya Patel: functionally similar. Dedicated gives you isolated capacity, predictable latency and allows you to pin versions and quantization profiles tightly which can improve deterministic behavior. Hosted is faster to start and more elastic.
[03:31] Evan Carter: what's the expected latency delta between hosted quantized and dedicated high-perf?
[03:35] Carlos Ruiz: rough numbers: hosted general-purpose for 8k models ~100-200ms per short request; 32k native models often 400-700ms depending on hardware and length. Dedicated with GPU optimizations and int8 quantization can get that down 20-40% and offer much better tail latency. these are examples — we'll run benchmarks on your prompt set.
[03:57] Liam O'Connor: our SLO is 300ms median for interactive flows; will dedicated help meet that?
[04:02] Maya Patel: yes, with a medium-sized dedicated pool and tuned batching we can meet 300ms for short queries and consistent tails under 500ms. for 32k contexts latency for large requests will be higher, but we can offload via background batch jobs or stream partial outputs.
[04:18] Priya Sharma: let's talk cost — if we pick a 32k model hosted vs dedicated what's the per-token diff?
[04:24] Jordan Lee: high-level: hosted higher elasticity but higher per-token price for peak usage; dedicated is CAPEX-like committed spend with lower unit costs. exact numbers depend on model family and quantization. we'll send SKU pricing.
[04:36] Mei Wong: we also need SSO with SAML and RBAC so PMs and analysts have different access. is SSO supported in Hosted?
[04:43] Maya Patel: Hosted supports SSO for enterprise tiers; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed identity integrations and finer RBAC.
[04:50] Evan Carter: security and audit — can you export raw tokens or just metadata? we need redaction for PII, and to ensure no raw customer text leaves our environment for some regulated customers.
[04:59] Carlos Ruiz: Private on-prem is the only way we guarantee no data leaves infra. Dedicated can be configured with VPC and strict egress rules; Hosted encrypts and isolates data but as a managed service tokens are processed by Redwood infrastructure. we also offer automated PII redaction pipelines and middleware.
[05:16] Jordan Lee: Priya, can you share the top 20 example long-doc prompts after the call? that'll help us size the PoC.
[05:21] Priya Sharma: yes we'll upload a sample set and expected outputs.
[05:24] [05:25] Priya Sharma: (crosstalk) also want to confirm languages — we'll include Spanish and Japanese examples.
[05:30] Maya Patel: perfect. next I want to walk through a quick benchmark plan.
[05:33] Maya Patel: Plan: we run two lanes for 7 days: Hosted lane using the recommended hosted 32k model, Dedicated lane with a reserved pool and int8 quantized variant. We'll measure latency, cost/token, and JSON function-calling stability across languages.
[05:51] Evan Carter: how do you measure function-calling stability?
[05:54] Carlos Ruiz: metric is successful JSON parse rate, plus a drift rate for mismatched fields. we can add fuzz tests.
[05:59] Mei Wong: curious about prefix/KV caching — does that help with recency-sensitive docs?
[06:04] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood implements prefix KV caching and document-level caching to reduce repeated computation for similar reference context. for legal summarization where large shared context repeats, KV caching can cut cost significantly.
[06:16] Priya Sharma: does caching introduce consistency concerns if underlying doc changes?
[06:20] Carlos Ruiz: caches are versioned and invalidated when the doc changes; we tie to content hashes.
[06:25] Evan Carter: any constraints around model tool-calling and streaming together?
[06:29] Maya Patel: streaming plus function calling is supported; we stream token-by-token and can patch in function call signals. there's more complexity around partial function responses during streaming but it's doable.
[06:39] Jordan Lee: switching gears — compliance. SOC 2 in Hosted, Dedicated add-on for audit logs, Private for on-prem. Anything else you need?
[06:49] Liam O'Connor: we do penetration testing requirements and a third party attestation. can we get an external pen test report?
[06:55] Maya Patel: we can share summary reports and work with legal on scopes. for Dedicated/Private we can support customer-run pen tests in controlled windows.
[07:06] Priya Sharma: from ML perspective, we also need deterministic outputs for certain pipelines. are there models that are more deterministic?
[07:13] Carlos Ruiz: smaller models and quantized variants tend to be more repeatable, but prompt design + temperature settings are key. we also provide deterministic sampling and top-k controls for some models.
[07:25] Evan Carter: question — do you provide model eval tooling to run our datasets across models?
[07:29] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood Optimize has eval harnesses and we can run pairwise comparisons and show per-language metrics. part of the PoC we can include an eval batch run.
[07:40] Mei Wong: what's the onboarding timeline for a Dedicated cluster?
[07:44] Jordan Lee: typical is 2-6 weeks depending on region, networking, and custom integrations. Private on-prem is longer, often 6-12 weeks. Hosted is immediate.
[07:53] Priya Sharma: interesting. for the PoC we want both Hosted and Dedicated so we can compare. any constraints on the size of traffic we can simulate?
[07:59] Carlos Ruiz: we can simulate up to your expected peak and synthetic spiky traffic; we'll provision test capacity for the benchmark.
[08:07] Evan Carter: ok let's talk about sample numbers — our baseline 100k tokens/day increasing to 500k tokens/day. pricing model?
[08:15] Jordan Lee: we'll send pricing tiers for both hosted per-token and Dedicated reserved capacity options with example unit economics at 100k and 500k tokens/day.
[08:23] [08:24] Priya Sharma: any limits on languages for embeddings? we use multilingual search and a single vector index.
[08:30] Maya Patel: embeddings support multilingual models; embeddings quality varies per model — we can run similarity evals with your dataset.
[08:36] Liam O'Connor: technical question: how do you handle KV cache eviction and memory for 32k contexts?
[08:42] Carlos Ruiz: KV cache sharding and streaming evictions; on GPU runtime we map KV across hosts and stream in blocks. memory pressure is managed via chunking and prefetch heuristics. for Dedicated pools we size GPU RAM accordingly.
[08:56] Mei Wong: any experience with Arabic tokenization issues?
[08:59] Maya Patel: yes, some tokenizers split differently — we test and apply language-specific tokenization fixes. we'll include Arabic tests if you have samples.
[09:09] Evan Carter: ok good. Next — are there limits on function connectors? we plan to integrate with internal CRM, data warehouse and a secure retrieval layer.
[09:18] Carlos Ruiz: connectors are configurable; for sensitive connectors we recommend a retrieval layer inside your VPC and use signed ephemeral tokens. function-calling is proxied and logged.
[09:28] Priya Sharma: logging — do logs contain full prompt text? we need to redact PII.
[09:33] Maya Patel: logs can be configured to mask or redact sensitive fields; for Dedicated/Private you get full control.
[09:39] [09:40] Evan Carter: anything else on latency vs cost tradeoffs specific to 32k models we should consider?
[09:46] Carlos Ruiz: besides quantization int8/4, kernel selection, and batching windows, you can also do hybrid routing: short queries to small models and long docs to 32k models; using prefix caching for repeats will reduce cost.
[09:59] Mei Wong: from PM side, we need to show stakeholders a clear migration path if we start Hosted and later move to Dedicated.
[10:06] Jordan Lee: that's common — same API layer supports all three modes; you can lift-and-shift model pins and rollout policies.
[10:12] Priya Sharma: question — does Redwood support on-the-fly quantization profiling per model?
[10:17] Maya Patel: we provide recommended quantization profiles and can run model-specific int8/4 tests to verify accuracy/regression before enabling in Dedicated.
[10:26] Evan Carter: what's the failure mode for tool calls if external service is down?
[10:30] Carlos Ruiz: you can configure retries, fallbacks to cached data, or skip with partial results. we also allow circuit breakers to avoid cascading failures.
[10:39] Priya Sharma: ok let's capture immediate action items.
[10:42] Jordan Lee: Jordan to send pricing and Dedicated SKUs; Maya to create PoC runbook; Carlos to prepare benchmark template; customer to send prompts and network contacts.
[10:51] Evan Carter: sounds good.
[10:53] Mei Wong: one more question — for the PoC, can we run a restricted on-prem variant for a single high-sensitivity customer?
[10:59] Maya Patel: yes, that's where Private comes in; we can scope a limited on-prem pilot but it takes longer and we'd need ops alignment.
[11:08] Priya Sharma: timeline constraints — we want results in 3 weeks. is that feasible?
[11:12] Carlos Ruiz: 3 weeks is tight but possible for Hosted vs small Dedicated run for the baseline; deeper Private pilot would extend beyond that.
[11:20] Jordan Lee: we'll aim to have PoC plan in 3 business days and kickoff next week.
[11:26] Evan Carter: ok great. any regulatory concerns for EU customers we should flag?
[11:30] Maya Patel: just data residency and subject access requests; Dedicated in EU regions or Private is recommended.
[11:36] Mei Wong: thank you all.
[11:38] [11:40] Jordan Lee: recap of next steps: we'll share pricing, a PoC runbook, ask for sample prompts and languages, schedule deep-dive for VPC/KMS. I'll follow up with calendar invites.
[11:52] Priya Sharma: thanks y'all.
[11:54] Evan Carter: appreciate it.
[11:56] Meeting end.
